title: Nuevo Laredo Called to Defend Its 2027 Revenue Law Before State Congress Today
excerpt: Nuevo Laredo's representatives appear before the Tamaulipas Congress at noon today to defend the city's proposed 2027 revenue law.
content:
Nuevo Laredo's representatives are scheduled to appear before the Tamaulipas Congress at noon today, Tuesday, Nov. 24, to explain and justify the city's proposed 2027 revenue law — one of six municipalities summoned as the state legislature reviews all 43 municipal revenue laws for next year.

The Tamaulipas Congress began the review on Nov. 23 in a joint meeting of the Finance, Planning, Budget and Public Debt and Municipal Affairs commissions. Forty-two municipalities filed their initiatives within the legal deadline; Gómez Farías filed on Nov. 11, one day late. Six were summoned unanimously, on the proposal of Rep. Úrsula Patricia Salazar Mojica, president of the Municipal Affairs Commission: Tampico, Altamira, Ciudad Madero, Matamoros, Nuevo Laredo and Reynosa. The meetings are scheduled today in the Sala de Comisiones: Tampico at 10:00, Altamira at 10:30, Ciudad Madero at 11:00, Matamoros at 11:30, Nuevo Laredo at 12:00 and Reynosa at 12:30.

Nuevo Laredo's Cabildo unanimously approved the 2027 revenue law project on Nov. 6, in its 70th ordinary session, chaired by Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal. The project projects revenue of more than $5,169 million pesos to fund public services, programs and projects in 2027, and was sent to the state Executive and the Tamaulipas Congress for legislative review and final approval. It covers taxes, fees, products, aprovechamientos, plus federal and state participaciones and aportaciones. The proposal followed technical and financial analysis by the Treasury and Finance Secretariat, under criteria of responsibility, discipline and fiscal sustainability.

“En Nuevo Laredo tenemos muy claro que una administración responsable comienza con una buena planeación financiera,” Mayor Canturosas Villarreal said when the Cabildo approved the project.

In a separate, earlier step, Nuevo Laredo proposed a general 5% update to its cadastral — property-value — tables, plus a new classification for industrial land. Reynosa and Gustavo Díaz Ordaz proposed 10%, and Matamoros proposed 5% generally, plus 15% for private subdivisions. The commissions approved those proposals and applied a general 5% update to the other 39 municipalities. Finance Commission president Rep. Isidro Jesús Vargas Fernández stressed that the update is not a tax-rate increase — it updates the values used as the base for calculating property contributions. Protections cited for the cadastral update include fixed fees for popular-housing properties in 2026 UMA terms, early-payment discounts of up to 15% for commercial and industrial properties, plus a possible additional municipal stimulus of up to 5%, for a total discount of up to 20%, and a 50% property-tax discount for seniors. The stated aim is to reduce a roughly 19-year cadastral lag.

Rep. Salazar Mojica said the proposed changes “must have sufficient justification and observe the principles of tax legality, proportionality, equity and legal certainty.” Rep. Vargas Fernández said: “It is important to be clear that these updates do not imply an increase in taxes, nor in property-tax rates nor in the tax on real estate acquisition.”

After the six municipalities present their justifications today, the commissions will continue their analysis and draft committee reports, which then go to the full legislature for consideration and a vote. The outcome of today's meetings was not yet public when this story was published.

Sources:

  • Congreso de Tamaulipas, Nov. 23, 2026
  • Reporte Tamaulipas, Nov. 6, 2026
  • Congreso de Tamaulipas, Boletín 11033
